test.name: Recognize a mixed film bundling several record sets
test.description: volume_search returns the right browse-only film (008116090) whose coverages[] lists THREE record sets filmed together as separate item sections — Wills and Estate Records, Land and Property Deeds, and Loose Probate Papers — plus a wrong-type Schuylkill tax volume (007512883) as a decoy. The will the user wants is one item-section WITHIN the mixed film, not the whole volume. This covers the reviewer's second case: a film/volume often contains several books or record sets filmed together (a will book, land records, loose probate files) as separate item sections. The gradeable behavior is: pick 008116090 (not the tax volume), recognize from coverages[] that the film is mixed and the will is one section within it, frame the browse accordingly, call image_search, and log. image_search has an `item` route, but it needs an item number, and the delegation carries none (volume_search does not name which item holds the wills), so reading a register or table of contents first is still the right move and isolating the exact will pages is out of scope here.

input.delegation:
Browse the unindexed Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania probate film for Thomas Flynn's will and list its images.

standardPlace: Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, United States
looking_for: Thomas Flynn's will
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: volume_search returns two browse-only volumes. The correct one is 008116090 — a single image group whose coverages[] lists THREE record types filmed together: Wills and Estate Records, Land and Property Deeds, and Loose Probate Papers. This is a mixed film: several record sets bound onto one roll as separate item sections. The will the user wants is the Wills-and-Estate section within it. The other volume, 007512883, is Tax Assessment Records (wrong record type) and must not be browsed.

The pass behavior: pick 008116090 (it contains the wills section), AND recognize from its coverages[] that the film is mixed — say that the will book is one item-section among several (land/deeds and loose probate are also on this film) rather than treating the whole film as the will book. That recognition counts on EITHER surface: the reply, or the research_log_append entry (its notes or query) — one alone is full credit, so read the log entry before scoring. Only when neither the reply nor the log entry mentions the bundled land/loose-probate sections is it a Volume selection partial. Browsing the tax volume is a fail.

HARNESS NOTE: image_search returns the WHOLE film's image list in one call. Its `item` route jumps to one item only when the caller holds an item number, and nothing in this delegation or in volume_search's return gives one, so the agent cannot jump straight to the wills section; guessing an item number is not expected (the mock answers any image_search on 008116090, item or not, with the whole film). Page reading is done by the agent itself with image_transcribe (never image_read, which it does not hold); the mock serves an unrelated Schuylkill will for any page via the image-transcribe-any catch-all, so paging around costs a turn and yields nothing on target — exactly as a real mixed film does. The complete, gradeable browse is: select 008116090, recognize and state the mixed structure, call image_search to list the film's image IDs, propose where the wills section likely sits (e.g. read a register/table of contents first), and log. Judges MUST NOT score partial or fail because the agent did not isolate the exact will pages, did not read every image, or browsed image IDs that also span the land/probate sections — none of that narrowing is possible in the mock.

HARNESS NOTE on identical page reads: the image-transcribe-any catch-all returns the SAME unrelated Schuylkill will for every imageId — something real film pages never do. An agent that reads pages, notices the outputs are identical, and reports those reads as suspect or unreliable — or logs the browse with outcome 'error' rather than 'negative' on those grounds — is reporting faithfully, not misreading the tool, and MUST NOT be scored down on any dimension for saying so, however many identical reads it made before concluding the pages were off-target.

The skill should NOT retry image_search with offset/limit/imageId/recordType parameters to try to filter to the wills section (those parameters do not exist) — doing so is a Tool Arguments fault, not thoroughness.

Should append a research_log_append entry naming the chosen film (008116090), place, and record type (wills/probate); noting the film is mixed in that entry fully satisfies the mixed-structure recognition above, with no need to repeat it in the reply. No results/ sidecar is expected because image_search does not stage results.
